newsitem.title: SPAIN: Endesa denies breaking CMNV regulations.
newsitem.headline: Endesa denies breaking CMNV regulations.

text.p: Spanish electricity firm Endesa denied on Thursday that it had violated CMNV stock market commission rules.
Endesa said in a note that it trusted the case would "conclude finally with the total exoneration of responsibility by the firm and its management."
The CNMV said late on Wednesday that it would start proceedings against Endesa, its chairman and its finance director for a "very serious infraction" of bourse regulations.
Endesa had failed to tell the authority about its plans to bid for 75 percent of regional utilities Fuerzas Electricas de Catalunya (Fecsa) and Sevillana de Electricidad in October, the CNMV said.
The firm may have to face a heavy fine, the bourse authority said.
Endesa said it had yet to receive any formal communication from the commission of the charges.
The firm said it had "scrupulously met its obligation to communicate relevant facts" to the CNMV regarding its bid for the two companies and denied having hidden "any concrete plan" to make an offer.
"The specification and adoption of such a decision would not have been made, nor was it legally possible for Endesa, given its condition as a state-owned firm" it said.
The infraction was due "only to a different interpretation of the information by the CNMV and by Endesa", it added.

"It should be highlighted that there has not been at any moment accounting or financial irregularities...nor use of privileged information from this company from which any third person could benefit," the firm said.
